title: Decisions, markets and the circular flow
subtitle: Engineers choose between alternatives with limited money. Economics supplies the language: scarcity, demand, supply and the flow of income.

scarcity.title: Scarcity and the economic decision
scarcity.body: Resources (money, time, materials) are limited while wants are not: that is scarcity. Every choice has an opportunity cost — the value of the best alternative given up. Engineering economics compares the monetary consequences of technical alternatives so that the option giving the most benefit per unit of resource is chosen.
scarcity.steps: You can spend Rs 100,000 on machine A (return Rs 12,000/yr) or machine B (return Rs 15,000/yr). Choosing A gives up B’s extra return. Opportunity cost of A per year:

proc.title: The decision process
proc.body: A rational engineering decision follows steps: define the problem, list alternatives (including “do nothing”), estimate cash flows, choose a criterion (present worth, IRR …), compare, consider non-monetary factors, decide, and review the result afterwards.

demand.title: Demand and supply
demand.body: The law of demand: as price rises, quantity demanded falls. The law of supply: as price rises, quantity supplied rises. Where the curves cross is the equilibrium: price and quantity at which the market clears. If the price is above equilibrium there is a surplus and sellers cut prices; below it, a shortage and prices rise.
demand.steps: Demand Qd = 110 − 2P; supply Qs = 2P − 10. Set them equal. 4P = 120, so P = 30 and Q = 50.

elastic.title: Elasticity
elastic.body: Price elasticity of demand E = (%ΔQ)/(%ΔP). |E| > 1: elastic (quantity reacts strongly — luxuries, substitutes available); |E| < 1: inelastic (necessities). A firm facing elastic demand raises revenue by cutting price; with inelastic demand, by raising it.
elastic.steps: Price rises from 20 to 22 (+10 %); quantity falls from 100 to 85 (−15 %). E = −15/10 = −1.5, so |E| > 1: elastic.

gdp.title: National income and the circular flow
gdp.body: Households supply labour and buy goods; firms hire labour and sell goods; money flows round. GDP = the market value of final goods and services produced in a country in a year; three equal ways to measure it: production (value added), income (wages + profit + rent + interest) and expenditure: GDP = C + I + G + (X − M).
gdp.steps: C = 600, I = 200, G = 150, exports 120, imports 90 (all in billions). GDP = 600 + 200 + 150 + (120 − 90).

infl.title: Inflation, growth and real values
infl.body: Inflation is a general rise in prices. Real GDP divides nominal GDP by a price index to remove it. A nominal interest rate i relates to the real rate r and inflation f by (1 + i) = (1 + r)(1 + f). Ignoring inflation makes future money look bigger than it is.
